text:
AzureCorp: Hey team — after IdP key rotation this morning a subset of our users (EU region) can't sign in. They get bounced back to /login?error=invalid_saml and 403 on SAML POST. Started ~09:12 UTC. Ticket SUP-9218.

support_jane: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the raw SAMLResponse (base64) snippet or the SP logs for the POST? Also a curl reproducer if possible.

AzureCorp: Here's a quick curl we used to repro from our test lab:
```
curl -v -X POST https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ 
  --data-urlencode "SAMLResponse=PHNhbWwtcmVzcG9uc2U... (truncated)"
*   Trying 10.1.2.3...
* Connected to app.redwood.example (10.1.2.3) port 443 (#0)
> POST /saml/acs HTTP/1.1
> Host: app.redwood.example
> Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
> Content-Length: 12345
>
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
< content-length: 210
< x-request-id: 8b2f3a
<
{
  "error": "invalid_saml",
  "reason": "Destination mismatch: https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs"
}
```

support_jane: Thanks — that Destination mismatch message is from our SAML validation layer. Two quick things to check: (1) the ACS in the decoded SAMLResponse exactly matches the SP-configured ACS (including trailing slash and port), (2) cookie domain and SameSite config — afterwards users report being dropped back to the login page (cookie not persisted).

eng_sre_miguel: I pulled the SP logs for the x-request-id 8b2f3a. Relevant excerpt:
```
time=2026-03-10T09:12:17Z level=warn msg="saml validation failed" req=8b2f3a error="destination mismatch: got https://login.azurecorp.com/SAML2/POST, expected https://app.redwood.example/saml/acs"
time=2026-03-10T09:12:17Z level=info msg="found signing cert by thumbprint old-thumb-1, verification ok"
time=2026-03-10T09:12:17Z level=info msg="metadata last fetch: 2026-03-10T05:00:00Z (poller)"
```

eng_sre_miguel: Two oddities: the SAMLResponse Destination is the IdP's POST endpoint (login.azurecorp.com/SAML2/POST) rather than our ACS, and our metadata poller last fetched at 05:00 UTC (pre-rotation). It looks like IdP rotated keys and also changed their outbound Destination/RelayState behavior.

devops_kate: @eng_sre_miguel can you confirm whether we accept ACS urls with/without trailing slash and whether we normalize hostnames (www vs non-www)? We had a normalization change in the ACS matcher last quarter.

eng_sre_miguel: We do normalize by path but we treat the full Destination (scheme+host+path) as authoritative. Legacy compatibility allowed host aliasing but that was tightened. I can temporarily relax strict Destination checking for this tenant if we want a hotfix.

AzureCorp: We did change our IdP SAML config during rotation: new signing key + changed AssertionConsumerService location (they started using their IdP-initiated flow and set Destination to their own POST endpoint). We didn't expect Destination to differ from SP ACS.

support_jane: Ok that's the root cause: IdP-initiated Destination points to IdP's post endpoint — SP rejects. Two mitigation paths:
- Short term: we can relax Destination check for this tenant (allow destination==IdP_post or our ACS) and push a safe config change.
- Customer action: update IdP to set Destination == SP ACS (recommended).

oncall_mark: For the relaxation option I need an audit trail. @support_jane please confirm we have customer's signed consent (they did in the ticket). I'll also add a short-lived feature flag for 24h and watch metrics.

support_jane: Confirmed — AzureCorp approved the temporary relax. I'm going to apply it and watch the rollout.

bot-metadata-watch: Metadata poller detected change for idp://azurecorp.example/entity at 2026-03-10T09:18:03Z — new signingKey thumbprint new-thumb-2, old-thumb-1 still valid in metadata.

eng_sre_miguel: Good — metadata now contains both keys. However the cookie issue remains for some EU users: their session cookie isn't being set after SAML POST. Logs show Set-Cookie but browser drops it. Suspect SameSite or cookie domain mismatch introduced by the customer's proxy -> we saw Host header rewrite on certain requests. Sample header from repro:
```
Host: app.redwood.example
X-Forwarded-Host: login.azurecorp.com
X-Forwarded-Proto: https
Cookie: <none>
```

devops_kate: If X-Forwarded-Host is set to IdP host and our cookie domain logic uses request host we might be setting cookie for login.azurecorp.com which the browser won't send back for app.redwood.example — that explains missing cookie. I'll instrument the cookie domain resolver and roll a fix to prefer configured SP host for cookie domain, ignoring X-Forwarded-Host.

support_jane: Action items:
- eng_sre_miguel: applied Destination-relax flag for tenant (24h).
- devops_kate: roll cookie-domain fix to prefer configured SP host (hotfix; CL 4392).
- AzureCorp: please set IdP to use SP ACS for IdP-initiated flow and avoid rewriting Host header in your proxy (or preserve Host).

AzureCorp: Thanks — we'll push IdP change and adjust proxy. Will confirm when users can login.

oncall_mark: Monitoring: set alert for increased 403 on /saml/acs and spike in unauthenticated redirects. Rolling back Destination relax if we see anomalies.

support_jane: Follow-up: after metadata poller saw new-thumb-2, we validated signatures from both keys. Destination-relax + cookie fix should cover both symptom classes (Dest mismatch + cookie host rewrite). I'll update ticket SUP-9218 and close once AzureCorp confirms. :white_check_mark:
